meta.title: Spanish general elections
sources: Wikipedia: Spanish general election articles, 1867–2023 (results, infoboxes and leads)
Interior Ministry and Junta Electoral figures as reported there

eras.label: Revolution and the Sexenio
eras.blurb: The last Isabelline election of 1867 was followed by the Glorious Revolution: the 1869 vote, held under universal male suffrage, was among Europe's most democratic to date, and the turbulent Sexenio ran through a monarchy-by-invitation to the First Republic's brief life.

eras.label: The Restoration and the turno pacífico
eras.blurb: For half a century the Conservative and Liberal parties alternated in power by arrangement — the turno pacífico. The Interior Ministry's encasillado assigned winners before polling day, with rural bosses, the caciques, delivering the count. The recorded majorities are the system's product, not the voters'.

eras.label: The Second Republic
eras.blurb: The Republic's three elections were mass democracy at last — women voted from 1933 — and each swung violently: a republican-socialist chamber, then a right-wing one, then the Popular Front's narrow 1936 victory, five months before the coup that began the Civil War.

eras.label: The Francoist Cortes
eras.blurb: Franco's 'organic democracy' allowed heads of family to elect a small fraction of a corporatist Cortes, with no parties and no opposition. These votes are recorded here as rituals of the dictatorship, not elections.

eras.label: The democratic era
eras.blurb: The 1977 election — the first free vote in 41 years — anchored the transition, and the 1978 Constitution followed. Since then: González's 1982 landslide, the peaceful alternations of PSOE and PP, the end of the two-party duopoly after 2015, and the coalition politics of the 2019–2023 chambers.

elections.summary: A general election was held in Spain from 10 to 13 March 1867 to elect the members of the 10th Cortes under the Spanish Constitution of 1845. 352 seats in the Congress of Deputies were up for election. Less than 400,000 people were eligible to vote, about 2.6% of the total population.

A general election was held in Spain from 15 to 18 January 1869 to elect the members of the Constituent Cortes in the Democratic Sexennium period. 363 of 381 seats in the Cortes were up for election. In the Canary Islands the election was held from 27 to 30 January, in Puerto Rico it was held from 30 May to 1 June, and in Cuba it was indefinitely postponed.

A general election was held in Spain from 8 to 11 March 1871 to elect the members of the 1st Cortes under the Spanish Constitution of 1869, during the Democratic Sexennium period. 406 of 424 seats in the Congress of Deputies and all 200 seats in the Senate were up for election.

elections.label: April 1872
elections.summary: A general election was held in Spain from 2 to 5 April 1872 to elect the members of the 2nd Cortes under the Spanish Constitution of 1869, during the Democratic Sexennium period. 406 of 424 seats in the Congress of Deputies and all 200 seats in the Senate were up for election. The election in Cuba was indefinitely postponed.

elections.label: August 1872
elections.summary: A general election was held in Spain from 24 to 27 August 1872 to elect the members of the 3rd Cortes under the Spanish Constitution of 1869, during the Democratic Sexennium period. 406 of 424 seats in the Congress of Deputies and all 200 seats in the Senate were up for election. The election in Cuba was indefinitely postponed.
The election was held with universal male suffrage. It was held in very unorthodox conditions and drew a very low voter turnout, as neither the Carlist or Alfonsist monarchists participated.

A general election was held in Spain from 20 to 23 January 1876 to elect the members of the Constituent Cortes in the Restoration period. 406 of 424 seats in the Congress of Deputies and all 200 seats in the Senate were up for election.
elections.caveat: A turno pacífico election: the result was largely arranged in advance through the Interior Ministry's encasillado and enforced locally by caciques. The recorded majorities describe the system, not free voting.

elections.summary: General Primo de Rivera, who had run a military dictatorship in Spain since 1923, resigned as head of government in January 1930. There was little support for a return to the pre-1923 system, and the monarchy had lost credibility by backing the military government.

elections.knownAs: Women vote for the first time
elections.summary: Elections to Spain's legislature, the Cortes Generales, were held on 19 November 1933 for all 473 seats in the unicameral Cortes of the Second Spanish Republic. Since the previous elections of 1931, a new constitution had been ratified, and the franchise extended to more than six million women.
Legislative elections were held in Spain on 16 February 1936. At stake were all 473 seats in the unicameral Cortes Generales.

General elections were held in Spain on 10 October 1967 where Spanish citizens elected 102 of the 564 members of the Cortes Españolas, the Spanish legislature. It was the first election held in Spain since the 1936 general election before the Spanish Civil War (1936–1939) and the first general election held during the dictatorship of Francisco Franco.
elections.caveat: A Francoist 'organic democracy' vote: no parties, no opposition, and only a fraction of a corporatist Cortes elected by heads of family. Recorded here as a ritual of the dictatorship, not an election.

elections.summary: To be eligible to vote, citizens must be heads of families, married women, or widows. To be eligible to be a candidate, citizens must be born in a province they are running in, have resided in the province for at least seven years since the age of 14, be supported by 1,000 electors of 0.5 percent of the province's population, and be a member of the National Movement.
elections.caveat: A Francoist 'organic democracy' vote: no parties, no opposition, and only a fraction of a corporatist Cortes elected by heads of family. Recorded here as a ritual of the dictatorship, not an election.

elections.knownAs: The first free vote in 41 years
elections.summary: It was the first free election held in Spain since 1936, prior to the outbreak of the Spanish Civil War. It was called by Prime Minister Adolfo Suárez as part of the political reform of the Francoist regime, ongoing since shortly after Francisco Franco's death in 1975 and promoted by his successor, King Juan Carlos I.

A general election was held in Spain on 1 March 1979 to elect the members of the 1st Cortes Generales under the Spanish Constitution of 1978. All 350 seats in the Congress of Deputies were up for election, as well as all 208 seats in the Senate.

A general election was held in Spain on 22 June 1986 to elect the members of the 3rd Cortes Generales under the Spanish Constitution of 1978. All 350 seats in the Congress of Deputies were up for election, as well as 208 of 254 seats in the Senate.

A general election was held in Spain on 29 October 1989 to elect the members of the 4th Cortes Generales under the Spanish Constitution of 1978. All 350 seats in the Congress of Deputies were up for election, as well as 208 of 254 seats in the Senate.

Felipe González's third term in office had seen Spain completing projects like the Madrid–Seville high-speed rail line and hosting events such as the Seville Expo '92 and the Barcelona '92 Summer Olympics, which contributed to the modernization of the country's international image.
